about: The dated facts about AI video models that stage.py compile, the GEN checks and the estimate use (blueprint 8.2). Facts from C1 (models, prices, controls), C3 (prompt syntax per model) and D3 (voice routes), all checked 2026-09-27. Refresh them with stage.py refresh-models before money is spent when they are more than model_facts_max_age_days old.
how_to_read: One entry per model, keyed by its exact name; 'aliases' are the other names people use ("Kling O3" = kling-3.0-omni). Code finds a model by its name or any alias, ignoring case (blueprint 5.7).

length_s: {min, max, step} (every length from min to max in steps) or {allowed: [...]}; forced_<n>_when lists the settings that force an n-second clip (Veo: 1080p, 4K or reference pictures force 8 s). Only {max} means the shortest clip is not known, so code does not check the length against it.
resolution and shapes: the picture sizes and frame shapes the model makes; code generates at an allowed shape and crops to the film's frame shape (K24).

inputs: what the model accepts. audio_reference: the model takes a line's recording (voices first, K16). voice: how a voice is fixed for this model. guide_video: whether a grey preview video can steer the camera and blocking.
audio: 'native' (made with the picture), 'native, switchable', or 'none' for a silent model (GEN-08 reads it).

adapter, order, time_marker, end_state, speaker, speaker_quotes, reference_tag, single_shot, camera_static: the model's own word order and syntax (C3 §16); the compiler follows them. speaker is a template with {who}, {delivery}, {description} and {line}; speaker_quotes false means the line is never in quotation marks (GEN-09).

prompt_limit: a verified hard limit in characters, tokens (words x the tokens-per-word estimate) or words (GEN-01). prompt_limit_unverified: a limit the research could not confirm; the compiler keeps under it where it can and says so, and the checker does not enforce it.

price_usd_per_s: dollars per generated second by resolution ('720p'), by sound ('audio', 'silent', 'voice_control') or 'default'; a [low, high] pair is a range across routes, priced at its high end. Prices come from the date in checked_on; above model_facts_max_age_days no pack is marked paid and no money is printed (GEN-11).

status: current, test_first (new or untested: two cheap test takes first) or retired (then it is only in the 'retired' list, with its replacements). use: generation, edit, performance_transfer or talking_head.
licensed_data: true only for models trained on licensed footage (PROJECT licensed_data_only routes only to these).

marks: one mark per fact: V verified (a maker's page or two agreeing sources, as the research file says), U unverified, J judgement, with the research file, section and source number. sources: the pages to re-read when refreshing (stage.py refresh-models).

kind: route marks an entry that is a model plus the place it runs (route_of names the model), such as minimax-h3-comfyui-r2v. A route is never chosen automatically: compile makes its clip book only when asked (compile --route, or PROJECT video_route). Its frames, tail_s_min, sizes, settings (by the tool's own box names), troubleshooting and rules (each with its kit mark and check) are read by clip_book.py and checks_clip_book.py.

rule_marks_from_takes.how: a rule is confirmed when at least takes_to_confirm takes say confirmed and none says wrong; wrong when at least takes_to_drop takes say wrong and more say wrong than confirmed; otherwise it keeps its kit mark. Verified or confirmed: its check is an error; unclear: a warning, shown as a suggestion; wrong: not run, listed on the take log page as dropped.

settings.why: Lightning is a 4-step turbo mode with slightly lower sound and motion quality; it can make movement stiff.

settings.set: 20 (the default); 25 for a clip where a face carries the moment
settings.why: 20 steps is the template's default and more steps are offered; testers found more steps move better.

settings.set: delete the two wires from this box into the MiniMax H3 box (width and height), then type the width and height on the H3 box
settings.why: the template starts at a small preview size; the clip pages give the full and the test size.

settings.set: the seconds given under each clip, for example 11.5 for 277 frames
settings.why: the template rounds the seconds up to the next length H3 makes (17 x k + 5 frames); typing a clip's exact seconds can tip it into a longer length with no prompt behind the extra part.
max keeps the pictures up to 2048 pixels on the short side, so faces stay closer to your pictures; it is slower.

settings.set: a fixed seed while testing; for a clip with speech, run 2 or 3 seeds and keep the clean one
settings.why: one change at a time tells you something; testers found the timing of speech follows the seed.

settings.set: the clip's prompt, from the line after COPY FROM HERE to the line before COPY TO HERE
settings.why: the prompt names the pictures by number, which is how the Reference to Video template reads them.

troubleshooting.first_change: check Lightning is off; use 25 steps; check the start picture shows people in the middle of doing something; search the prompt for a word asking for stillness; then run another seed

troubleshooting.symptom: The motion is in slow motion
troubleshooting.first_change: run another seed; then use 25 steps

troubleshooting.symptom: Speech is wrong: the wrong mouth, a line said twice, mumbled or extra words
troubleshooting.first_change: change the seed first and run 2 or 3 seeds; change words only after that

troubleshooting.symptom: The wrong people, or an extra person
troubleshooting.first_change: look at the start picture and the connected pictures first: a connected person's picture makes them appear
set ref_image_size to max; use a clearer, bigger face in the character picture; check each description is pasted exactly (rewording re-rolls the face)

troubleshooting.symptom: A contact goes wrong: the thing breaks before it is hit, or on its own
troubleshooting.first_change: trim that shot to end earlier; the next shot already shows the result

troubleshooting.symptom: A cut lands in the wrong place
troubleshooting.first_change: cuts can land about a second late and lines start up to a second and a half late: trim by what you see; if a shot is squeezed out, run another seed

troubleshooting.symptom: The picture breaks up at the end
troubleshooting.first_change: that is the tail: trim it; if it breaks up before the keep point, check the length typed in Float (Duration)
take it out of the start picture, and check the prompt does not name it

troubleshooting.symptom: The camera moves in a clip with cuts
troubleshooting.first_change: run another seed; never add more camera lines, which testers found made it worse
run it again, or lay the words in during the edit as a text graphic

minimax-h3-comfyui-r2v.price_note: the time on your own or a rented computer; not priced here

rules.says: The prompt has six sections in MiniMax's order, each starting on its own line: subject_definitions, summary, retention_analysis, detailed_description, overall_soundscape, non_diegetic_music.
There is one <Picture N> label for each picture connected, numbered in the order the pictures are connected (the start picture is <Picture 1>), and no more than 9 pictures.
rules.source: MiniMax H3 reference-mode prompt guide, https://huggingface.co/MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-H3/blob/main/docs/VIDEO_PROMPT_WRITING_GUIDE_ref_en.md; ComfyUI MiniMax H3 templates and settings, https://docs.comfy.org/tutorials/video/minimax/minimax-h3-native

rules.says: Every <Subject N> the prompt uses is defined in subject_definitions.
Every person whose picture is connected is placed in a shot: a connected picture makes that person appear.
rules.source: Project notes 42 (the handover) and 43 (the build plan); the clip file's traps

rules.says: Speakers are numbered (S1), (S2) in the order they first speak, and no speaker number is written in retention_analysis.
Every spoken line is inside <d>[Language] ... </d>, with the tags balanced.
The spoken lines are the story's lines, word for word, and none is left out because the story's speeches are missing.
rules.source: Stage: the story's lines are sent word for word (blueprint 8.1); MiniMax H3 reference-mode prompt guide, https://huggingface.co/MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-H3/blob/main/docs/VIDEO_PROMPT_WRITING_GUIDE_ref_en.md

rules.says: [Shot 1] has no time; each later shot opens '[Shot N] At 00:04.500,' (minutes and seconds, to the thousandth) and the times rise from 0.
One 'From ... to the end' line of small actions starts inside the last shot, before the keep point, so the tail is never empty.
rules.source: h3-storyboard testing notes, https://github.com/phileiny/h3-storyboard-skill (skills/h3-storyboard/SKILL.md); Project notes 42 (the handover) and 43 (the build plan)

rules.says: Nothing is timed in the tail, and the tail after the keep point is at least 1.3 seconds: H3 often breaks up 1.2 to 1.7 seconds before the end. No two lines are timed over each other, and each line ends at least a second before the keep point, because H3 starts lines 1.4 to 1.9 seconds late.
The clip's length in frames is on the 17 x k + 5 grid at 24 frames a second, with a one-decimal value to type that lands on it.
rules.source: ComfyUI MiniMax H3 templates and settings, https://docs.comfy.org/tutorials/video/minimax/minimax-h3-native

rules.says: The clip's length is between 124 and 362 frames (the template's default and 15 seconds snapped up on the grid; shorter lengths on the grid are untested).
rules.source: ComfyUI MiniMax H3 templates and settings, https://docs.comfy.org/tutorials/video/minimax/minimax-h3-native; Project notes 42 (the handover) and 43 (the build plan)

rules.says: H3 makes at most 15 seconds, so a held take longer than that, with its tail, cannot be made as planned: the rest is made in the edit or the shot is redesigned.
detailed_description is about 350 to 500 words (MiniMax: 'normally'); under 200 or over 700 is reported.

Outside the spoken lines and printed words, no word that names something absent (no, not, nothing, never, none ...): H3 in ComfyUI has no negative side, and naming a thing adds it. The one exception is 'with no camera movement whatsoever'.
rules.source: ComfyUI MiniMax H3 prompt guide, https://docs.comfy.org/tutorials/video/minimax/minimax-h3-prompt-guide; h3-storyboard testing notes, https://github.com/phileiny/h3-storyboard-skill (skills/h3-storyboard/SKILL.md)

rules.says: Outside the spoken lines, no word that asks for stillness (still, frozen, does not move ...): people are written as small timed actions.
Outside the spoken lines, no talk about speaking (sentence, words, speaks, asks, answers ...): H3 may say it aloud. Only 'says' right before a line, which the code writes, is allowed.
Outside the spoken lines, no comparison ('like a ...', 'as if'): H3 may draw the thing compared.
A static clip has one camera sentence, 'static, on a tripod, with no camera movement whatsoever', and no camera-move words.
Each person's fixed description and state line are written word for word next to their label: rewording re-rolls the face.
rules.source: MiniMax H3 reference-mode prompt guide, https://huggingface.co/MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-H3/blob/main/docs/VIDEO_PROMPT_WRITING_GUIDE_ref_en.md; Project notes 42 (the handover) and 43 (the build plan)

rules.says: detailed_description opens with the style sentence made from the film's style words.
rules.source: Project notes 42 (the handover) and 43 (the build plan)

rules.says: The start picture brief says who is in the picture ('... are the only people in the picture', or '... is deserted').
rules.source: Project notes 42 (the handover) and 43 (the build plan)

rules.says: A clip holds one to three shots and at most four people's pictures; a long shot made in parts has no moment running across the cut between two parts.
rules.source: Project notes 42 (the handover) and 43 (the build plan)

rules.says: Two shots cut together in one clip differ clearly in size (two steps or more), angle or setup, or the second is an insert: a cut between similar framings can be smoothed away.
Two singles of two people facing each other share a clip only after a shot showing both in that clip; otherwise each single is a clip of its own.
A contact (one thing driven into another, then the result) is never shown inside one shot: cut at the contact and open the next shot on the result, with the sound on the cut.
rules.source: h3-storyboard testing notes, https://github.com/phileiny/h3-storyboard-skill (skills/h3-storyboard/SKILL.md); Project notes 42 (the handover) and 43 (the build plan)

rules.says: Every clip page names its master picture and its character pictures, and says in plain words which part of the mirror world it cannot make safely.
rules.source: Project notes 42 (the handover) and 43 (the build plan)

strengths: no rewriting step between your words and the model: the prompt is read as written
up to 9 reference pictures tied to the prompt by numbered labels
weaknesses: the last 1.2 to 1.7 seconds of a clip often break up (testers)
contact between things (a hit, a push) is unreliable on screen (testers)
a negative prompt has no effect
